turns.speaker: a
turns.text: So the plan is to deploy the new release to the staging cluster on Tuesday.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: We deploy to staging first, then production on Thursday if nothing breaks.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: And the rollback? If the deploy goes wrong on Thursday, what happens?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: We keep the previous release running, so a rollback is just a switch.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: The other thing is, well, the other thing is what we are paying every month.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: The bill from the provider has gone up three times since January.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Three times? That is eating straight into our margin.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: It is. If it keeps climbing we cannot keep the current plan for the team.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: So we either move provider or we make the workers less hungry.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Last thing. We should hire another engineer before the next deploy cycle.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Agreed. Someone senior, who has run a platform team before.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I will write the job description this week and send it round.
